title: Prefetch crediting and ratecap heuristics for structured vector ops
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers are observing unpredictable token/embedding charges when our runtime performs speculative prefetches and background fanout for non-chat endpoints (embeddings, rerank, structured tool calls). Prefetches reduce latency, but current billing attributes costs immediately to the caller and applies hard quota consumption. This leads to customer-facing surprises (unexpected quota exhaustion, throttling) when prefetches are partially unused or rerouted to fallbacks.

Goal: Implement a conservative "soft credit" system and ratecap heuristics that: (1) attributes speculative prefetch costs in a reversible/temporary way, (2) protects hard quota windows from being permanently consumed by unused prefetches, and (3) reconciles final charges deterministically on completion or timeout. Also add ratecap heuristics so that bursty prefetch-driven fanout doesn't push customers into hard throttles while still preventing abuse.

Scope: Non-chat endpoints only (embeddings, rerank, structured output/toolcall invocations). Excludes streaming chat reservations. This ticket focuses on runtime metering + billing attribution; downstream invoicing and billing UI adjustments will be a follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: Speculative prefetches receive a soft credit entry that does not decrement the customer's hard quota immediately
On final success/failure, soft credits are reconciled: used tokens/embeddings become hard-charged; unused soft credits are released and do not contribute to billable counters
If a prefetch times out or is canceled due to routing/fallbacks, no hard charge remains and the reconciliation log is deterministic and auditable
Ratecap heuristics ensure customers with repeated speculative fanout are limited by a soft-window; metrics show <5% false-positive throttles in canary cohort
System exposes audit events for: soft-credit-create, soft-credit-convert, soft-credit-release, soft-credit-expire with request provenance and final attribution key
Unit and integration tests covering partial success (e.g., fanout where 2/5 subcalls return) with correct per-subcall attribution and billing events
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic with monitoring dashboards for mismatch between soft credits and final charges (target <0.1% mismatch after reconciliation delays)
Documentation (internal Confluence) describing the new soft-credit lifecycle and how billing/quotas will appear to customers
Backward compatibility: customers using legacy meter reconciliation (pre-2025-03) see identical final charges after reconciliation; no data-loss or double-charge incidents in canary
implementation_notes: Introduce a soft_credit table scoped per-customer + correlation_id. Fields: created_at, ttl, provisional_units, provisional_type (tokens|embeddings), provenance (prefetch|speculative_fanout), request_id
Soft credit created at request admission and charged to a transient ledger that is excluded from hard quota windows. TTL defaults to 30s for fanout-prefetch, configurable by policy per-route.

On completion we emit a reconciliation event: convert (amount) OR release (amount) depending on actual usage. Conversion atomically transfers units into the hard-ledger ensuring idempotency via correlation_id.

Add ratecap heuristic: sliding soft-window per-key that tracks provisional_units_created over last 60s. If provisional_units exceed soft_window_threshold (e.g., 2x expected steady rate), further prefetch attempts are rejected with a soft-429 that does not count toward hard throttle metrics.

Integrate with billing pipeline: soft-ledger events are written to same append-only stream used for invoicing but flagged as provisional. Downstream aggregator must reconcile provisional flags within 24h and only emit final billable events after conversion.

Edge case: cascading fallbacks. If primary prefetch fails and request re-routes to fallback model (different token cost), the reconciliation must convert only the subset of provisional units actually used by fallback path. Use per-subcall provenance to split soft credits.

Performance: keep soft credit operations O(1) and cheap; use in-memory LRU cache + persistent append for durability. Bench target: <0.5ms added p99 latency on admission for prefetch path on top of existing admission cost.

Auditability: reconciliation events include deterministic provenance: original_request_id, subcall_index, node_id, candidate_model_id, final_charge_units, and conversion_timestamp. This enables downstream refunds and claims.

Backfill safety: existing accounts with outstanding provisional entries from previous experiments must be reconciled before enabling canary. Provide a migration job that scans provisional flags and reconciles based on final logs.
Do not modify public token/embedding usage API responses for this rollout; customers may opt into preview via feature flag and per-account toggle in console
tradeoffs: Conservative TTL (30s) reduces risk of long-lived provisional charges but increases the chance of releasing useful prefetches — slightly higher latency on rare cold paths compared to unconditional hard charging
Implementing soft ledgers increases system complexity and state to track; tradeoff accepted to reduce customer-visible billing surprises and reduce support load
Ratecap heuristics may block legitimate bursty workloads; mitigated with a configurable per-account multiplier and telemetry-driven tuning during canary

Reconciliation latency introduces a window when billing is provisional (customers may see transient provisional counters). We limit exposure by surfacing only final counters in the billing UI and keeping provisional events internal

Durability vs latency: using an in-memory cache with append-only persistent log balances write latency and crash-safety. Complete durability requires no-ack path for append before conversion; we accept small risk but provide a nightly reconciliation job

comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Filed initial ticket after two customer incidents where prefetch fanout consumed embedding quotas within minutes. Summary + preliminary proposal attached to Confluence link.
2025-02-12 - Marcus Liu: Implementation spike shows soft-credit append adds ~0.35ms median and ~0.9ms p99. Will prototype eviction and persistent-append strategy.

2025-02-18 - Clara Moreno (PM): Finance reviewed and prefers provisional flags in billing stream to avoid double-charge complexity. Also requested an explainer for Support to handle customer inquiries.

2025-02-22 - Diego Ramos (Eng reviewer): Concern on correlation_id uniqueness across retries. Suggest use deterministic request hash + attempt counter; Marcus to implement idempotent conversion semantics.
2025-02-24 - Evan Brooks (Design): UX note — console should not show provisional charges to customers. Add internal view for support that lists provisional vs final events.

2025-03-01 - Marcus Liu: Canary started (5%). Early telemetry: provisional_create: 4.2M units, provisional_convert: 3.9M units, provisional_release: 0.3M units. Mismatch within expected bounds; no customer-facing quota complaints so far.
2025-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Billing and security signoff pending small changes to audit payload. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly. Moving to In Progress.
test_plan: Unit tests for soft credit lifecycle: create, convert, release, expire, idempotency for repeated conversion attempts
Integration test simulating 5-way fanout where 2 subcalls succeed and 3 fail; ensure final billed units equal only succeeded subcalls and that provisional release events are emitted for failures
Load test at production QPS showing <1ms additional p50 latency and <1.5ms p99 overhead for prefetch admission on a 16-core node
Canary observability tests: graphs for provisional_created vs provisional_converted, per-customer soft-window breach count, and false-positive throttle rate
Billing reconciliation test that runs nightly migration job against historical provisional events; assert no net change in final invoices for test accounts
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag and per-account toggle in console
Step 1 (Canary): 5% of hosted traffic for 48h with 24/7 oncall monitoring of billing-metrics channel
Step 2 (Ramp): 25% for 72h if canary metrics stable; finance to observe provisional->final delta
Step 3 (Opt-in): Offer preview opt-in for selected enterprise accounts to validate interop with Dedicated/Private deployments
Step 4 (Global): Gradual 100% rollout after 2 weeks of stable telemetry and signoff by Billing and Security
decision_log: 2025-02-13: Chosen soft-ledger approach over immediate token hold due to customer support cost projections and Finance preference
2025-02-22: Use 30s TTL by default after experiments showed 30s captured >98% of useful prefetch hits while limiting provisional window
2025-02-24: Ratecap implemented as soft-429 to avoid contaminating hard throttle metrics. Soft-429s are internal-only and surfaced to SDKs later if adopted
2025-03-01: Canary parameters set to 5% traffic and thresholds derived from historical embed burst percentiles (p95 x 1.5)
2025-03-03: Proceeding with In Progress; minor audit payload changes required before broader rollout
